title: Reserved + Burst Pricing experiments and enterprise questionnaire readiness for Dedicated
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary:
We need to define and validate a packaging and pricing model for Redwood Dedicated that balances predictable revenue (reserved GPU commitments), operational simplicity (autoscaling and burst policies), and enterprise procurement/security needs (contract questionnaire readiness, SLA tiers). This ticket coordinates pricing experiments, contract questionnaire deliverables, and the initial go/no-go for a two-tiered SLA offering (Standard / Premium).

Goals:
- Produce an experiment plan to test pricing and packaging variants for reserved capacity + burst credits + autoscaling policies with measurable unit economics.
- Complete draft answers to top 30 vendor security questionnaire items required by target enterprise prospects.
- Recommend initial SLA tiers and pricing bands for launch, align with legal/finance for contracting language.

Background / Motivation:
- Sales/SE feedback: enterprise prospects want predictable monthly costs (reserved GPUs) with headroom for traffic spikes (burst) and clear autoscaling behavior.
- Engineering: dedicated pools and autoscale are implemented but need clear billing semantics and SLO guardrails for burst.
- Finance: needs ARR forecasting assumptions for reserved commitments and rules to convert burst consumption into billable usage.

Primary hypotheses to test:
1) A hybrid offering (reserved baseline + prepaid burst credits) increases conversion from PoC to committed contracts vs. pure on-demand by >= 15%.
2) A soft-cap autoscaling policy with controlled burst (N minutes at X% over baseline) keeps 95th percentile token cost within 1.4x reserved baseline cost.
3) Two SLA tiers (Standard: 99.9% / Premium: 99.95% + faster support) will map to >60% of pilot customers selecting Standard and ~40% selecting Premium when price delta is ~20%.

Experiment matrix (planned):
- SKU axis: reserved vCPUs/GPUs (r1: 4xA10g, r2: 8xA10g, r3: 16xA100 equivalent), monthly price bands.
- Burst options: (B0) no burst, (B1) prepaid burst credits monthly, (B2) elastic burst with usage fees at X% premium.
- Autoscale policy: (A1) strict cap (no burst), (A2) soft cap with queued requests after grace, (A3) burst-first with fallback to compatible smaller model.
- SLA tiering: (S) Standard (99.9%, 24h incident response), (P) Premium (99.95%, 1h on-call).
We will run 6 canonical SKU combinations prioritized by sales interest.

Metrics / success criteria:
- Conversion lift: % of pilots converted to reserved contract across cohorts.
- Unit economics: cost per 1k tokens served (reserved vs burst) and 95th percentile cost multiplier.
- Revenue predictability: realized committed MRR / forecasted MRR variance <= 8%.
- Customer satisfaction: NPS / pilot CSAT >= targeted baseline.

Contract & Security questionnaire workstream:
- Deliverable: Draft answers for up to 30 enterprise questionnaire items that are repeatedly requested (data residency, encryption at-rest/in-transit, KMS integration, access controls, audit logs, incident procedures).
- Owner: Security & Compliance (Tariq Malik) for technical review; PM to draft language and coordinate legal.
- Timeline: initial draft by 2026-03-20, legal review by 2026-03-27, completed for sales pack by 2026-04-01.

Decisions made (so far):
- Pricing experiments will measure both prepaid burst credit subscription and on-demand burst pricing; we will NOT offer unlimited free burst for the first release.
- Autoscaling default policy for pilots: A2 (soft cap with brief grace period) to avoid surprising cost spikes while demonstrating elasticity.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should burst consumption be billed at a flat multiplier over reserved unit price or at a dynamic rate tied to cloud spot cost? (Finance prefers flat multiplier for predictability).
- How to represent partial month scaling/commits in contracts (pro-rate vs minimum term)? Legal prefers minimum monthly commit with pro-rated changes at month boundary.
- What enforcement mechanisms for burst to protect multi-tenant host capacity on Dedicated? (ENG-2145 investigating enforcement hooks).

Progress updates / recent activity:
- 2026-02-25: Kickoff with Sales, Finance, Legal, and Eng. Captured common buyer asks and sample procurement language.
- 2026-03-03: Engineering provided telemetry plan and costing model for reserved vs burst (ENG-2145).
- 2026-03-08: Draft experiment matrix and price bands shared with Growth for feedback (spreadsheet link: https://drive.redwood.example/dedicated-pricing-experiments).
- 2026-03-11: Security team provided canonical answers for encryption and KMS sections; pending legal sign-off on incident response wording.

Acceptance criteria for closing this ticket:
- Experiment matrix finalized and prioritized (owner-assigned) with instrumentation ready for A/B style measurement.
- Draft security questionnaire answers completed and reviewed by Security + Legal.
- Recommended pricing bands and SLA definitions documented and accepted by Finance + Sales leadership.
- Implementation tasks (billing hooks, billing UI, contract language) broken out into ENG work tickets with estimates.

Next steps / action items (owners):
- PM (Liam Chen): finalize experiment cohorts and briefing doc for pilot customers (due 2026-03-18).
- Security (Tariq Malik): finalize questionnaire draft and hand it to Legal (due 2026-03-20).
- Eng (owner ENG-2145): finalize burst enforcement and telemetry plan (ETA 2026-03-22).
- Finance: propose reserved discount tiers and burst multiplier that meet ARR targets (due 2026-03-19).

Links / artifacts:

- Draft pricing playbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood.example/dedicated-pricing-playbook
- Telemetry & costing PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/423

Stakeholders: Sales (Enterprise), Finance, Legal, Security & Compliance, Serving Runtime eng, Billing platform eng, Growth/Marketing.

Notes: Keep communication tight with the SLA/product ops owners — SLA promises will feed into Console uptime reports and legal SLAs. We should avoid overpromising availability until runtime telemetry for dedicated pools demonstrates consistent supportability at target percentiles.
